land.text: the whole Median realm, taken by Cyrus II: 'In 550 BC, the Median capital, Ecbatana, was conquered by the Persian king Cyrus II'

successors.note: Cliopatria's last Median shape is 551; its Achaemenid Empire shape starts in 550.

capitals.name: Ecbatana (Hamadan)
capitals.note: The infobox gives Ecbatana as the capital; Cyrus took it in 550 BC.

rulers.name: Cyaxares
rulers.note: Infobox, Herodotean chronology: Cyaxares 625-585 BC; accession dated 625 BC. The reign began ten years before Cliopatria's first shape (615).

rulers.name: Astyages
rulers.note: Infobox: Astyages 585-550 BC. Deposed when Cyrus took Ecbatana in 550.

correction.text: 'a territory stretching roughly from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River in Anatolia': the page puts the eastern limit in northeastern Iran, so Afghanistan and Pakistan (the shape reaches 72.8E, the Wakhan) are removed

keyframe_review.note: 2.06 M km2 against the Median dynasty infobox's 2.8 M km2 for 585 BC (ratio 0.74, inside the factor of two); about 1.35 M km2 remain after the correction (ratio 0.48 for the 615 outline, which has not yet reached the Halys). The shape is Iran (78 percent of it), Afghanistan (92 percent), south Turkmenistan and a corner of Pakistan: its Afghan third has no support on either page, which put the eastern limit in northeastern Iran, and Cyrus took Bactria, Arachosia and the rest only in 545-540 (Cyrus the Great page). The pages give no dates for Median control of Persia, Urartu or Manna, so the rest stands. Persis (Fars) is inside the shape but the Medes page calls Cyrus 'a Median vassal': drawn as vassal land by the ledger's vassal_start/vassal_end pair.

correction.text: 'a territory stretching roughly from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River in Anatolia' (the Halys): Cliopatria stops at about 43E, well east of the Halys; Anatolia up to the Halys is added (the Turkish part of Cliopatria's own 550 Achaemenid outline, whose west edge is 33.4E) and Afghanistan and Pakistan removed

keyframe_review.note: 2.24 M km2 against the infobox's 2.8 M km2 for 585 BC (ratio 0.80); the corrected outline is about 1.86 M km2 (ratio 0.66): Afghanistan and Pakistan out, Anatolia to the Halys in. The page says the Medes 'had eventually' reached the Kızılırmak after Assyria's fall, with no year; the west extension is drawn from -600 at confidence 1 in the ledger. The shape runs to -551; the year -550 belongs to the Achaemenid shape.

ledger.note: 615: the Median Kingdom appears on the map at Ecbatana, at war with Assyria. Cliopatria starts the state in 615; the page dates the dynasty from 700 BC (Deioces 700-678, 'Herodotus' chronology', which later scholars moved) and Cyaxares from 625 BC, and calls Deioces possibly only an eponymous founder; the year 615 is Cliopatria's, not the page's.

The Medes page calls Cyrus of Persia 'a Median vassal' in 553 BC but dates neither the start of the vassalage nor the Median conquest of Persia; Herodotus is said to credit Phraortes with subjugating the Persians (Median dynasty page), reign 678-625. Dated here to the start of the state's map life. The pre-550 Persian kingdom of Anshan is the core of the Achaemenid dossier. Reviewer me-05-a: counterpart is the pre-550 Persian kingdom of Anshan (no dossier); achaemenid-empire starts in 550.

616-609: the Medes and Babylonians destroy Assyria. 'attacked and destroyed the strife-riven Neo-Assyrian Empire between 616 and 609 BCE.' The span starts a year before the state's first map year; the zone is the researcher's reading, the pages do not name it.

region.text: the part of Assyria inside Cliopatria's 600 Median outline (the Zagros edge east of the Tigris)

ledger.note: 612: the Medes and Babylonians overthrow Assyria. 'By 612 BC, the Medes became strong enough to overthrow the declining Assyrian empire' in alliance with Babylonia. The page gives no partition between the two allies, so only the strip of Assyria that Cliopatria's 600 Median outline contains is drawn as a Median gain; Cliopatria gives the rest of the heartland to the Neo-Babylonian Empire from 600 and keeps a Neo-Assyrian shape to 601.
609: the end of Assyria. The Medes page's span for the destruction is 616-609 BCE ('Chaldean-Median coalition in 612-609 bce' in a reference note).

region.text: the western growth of Cliopatria's 600 outline over its 615 outline: Mannaean land in north-western Iran

ledger.note: The Medes page says the Mannaean states 'probably collapsed', which 'allowed Median groups to take over their territory', without a date; Cliopatria widens the outline in 600. Bridging only.

region.text: Anatolia east of the Kızılırmak (Halys), the Turkish part of Cliopatria's 550 Achaemenid outline

ledger.counterpart: Anatolian peoples east of the Halys
ledger.note: 'a territory stretching roughly from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River in Anatolia', reached after Assyria's fall; the page gives no year. Placed at 600 as the first year of the second Cliopatria shape. The page does not mention the Halys as a boundary with Lydia.
553: Cyrus revolts. 'In 553 BCE, Cyrus the Great, the King of Persia, a Median vassal, revolted against the Median king.' The page names Persia, not Fars or Anshan.

region.text: the Median heartland around Ecbatana, where the war was decided

ledger.note: 553-550: Cyrus against Astyages. 'The Chronicle suggests that the hostilities lasted for at least three years (553-550 BC),' ending in the capture of Ecbatana. The Cyrus page does not say where the fighting was; the zone is the researcher's reading.

550: Ecbatana falls. 'In 550 BC, the Median capital, Ecbatana, was conquered by the Persian king Cyrus II.' The Medes page: 'In 550 BCE, Cyrus finally won a decisive victory resulting in Astyages' capture'.

region.text: the whole Median realm, from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak

ledger.note: 550: the Medes lose their kingdom. 'In 550 BC, the Median capital, Ecbatana, was conquered by the Persian king Cyrus II' (the page); the Cyrus the Great page dates the 'overthrow of the Median kingdom' to 550 BC and gives 549-530 as his Median reign in the infobox.
550: the Median Kingdom ends; the Achaemenid Empire, Cyrus the Great's, begins on its land.

wars.name: Medo-Babylonian conquest of Assyria
wars.outcome: The Median and Chaldean coalition destroys the Neo-Assyrian Empire; the Medes page: 'attacked and destroyed the strife-riven Neo-Assyrian Empire between 616 and 609 BCE', and 612 for the overthrow (Median dynasty page).
wars.note: The war is the Babylonian side's as well; neither page divides the spoils. Cliopatria keeps a Neo-Assyrian shape to 601.

wars.name: Cyrus's revolt against Astyages
wars.outcome: Persian victory: Astyages captured and Ecbatana taken in 550; the Median kingdom passes to Cyrus.
wars.note: 'hostilities lasted for at least three years (553-550 BC)' per the Nabonidus Chronicle as the Cyrus page reports it; the Medes page dates the revolt to 553 and the decisive victory to 550.

certainty.note: No page gives a Median boundary; the only description is 'from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak River in Anatolia'. Every frontier is approximate.

notes: Pages opened: Median dynasty, Medes, Cyrus the Great (budget 1-2; the third is the Achaemenid dossier's page, cited for the 553-550 war). Not settled: (1) the founding year: the page dates the dynasty from 700 BC (Herodotus) and Cyaxares from 625, but the identity starts at Cliopatria's 615 so that the map and the dossier agree; a gap-filler may extend the life back with the page 'Medes' or 'Cyaxares' once the early chronology is chosen. (2) No page opened gives the Lydian war, the Battle of the Eclipse (585 BC) as a Median-Lydian battle, the Halys boundary treaty, or the date of Median control of Persia, Urartu or Manna; the Medes page does not mention the Halys or Lydia's border; pages to open: 'Battle of the Eclipse', 'Cyaxares', 'Fall of Nineveh', 'Siege of Harran'. (3) Cliopatria keeps the Neo-Assyrian Empire to 601 and Urartu to 551, although both pages say the Medes (with Babylonia) destroyed Assyria by 609: the Median shape and the Assyrian shape overlap in Cliopatria. (4) The 615 and 600 shapes include Afghanistan (92 percent of it) and a corner of Pakistan, reaching 72.8E; removed in the verdicts because the page puts the eastern limit in northeastern Iran and Cyrus took the east only in 545-540. Neither Cliopatria Median shape reaches Anatolia although the page says the realm ran to the Halys; added in the 600 verdict. (5) The Persian Cliopatria year: the Achaemenid dossier's 550 start is the Median end; Cyrus' kingdom of Anshan (559-550) is not a Cliopatria row. Cross-dossier points: the Neo-Assyrian Empire dossier already records the loss of Assur to the Medes in 615/614 and names this state as a successor (to 609); the Lydia dossier records a Median-Lydian contest in eastern Anatolia 590-585 ending with the Battle of the Eclipse (28 May 585): neither is mirrored here because neither page opened gives them; a gap-filler should add both from the pages those dossiers cite. Gazetteer names used: Media, Assyria, Persis (all in regions.jsonl). The Urartu question: Cliopatria keeps Urartu to 551 as a separate row and its Median outline never reaches the Armenian Highlands (it is Iran, Afghanistan and a corner of Turkmenistan), so no Median gain from Urartu is recorded. Reviewer me-05-a: the Median dynasty page also gives the realm as 'stretching from the eastern banks of the Halys River in Anatolia to Central Asia'; the removal of Afghanistan and Pakistan rests on the Medes page and on Cyrus' eastern campaigns of 545-540 (Cyrus the Great page), not on an explicit eastern limit.
